title: Christ the physician calls sinners
english: He calls the Lord Jesus a physician. He does not call the healthy but sinners. The herbs of the law are compounded in the school of the physician.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is opening a new homily, speaking in his own voice about Christ as a physician who calls sinners, not the healthy.

title: Birth of the stronger sense requires purification
english: “A woman who has conceived and borne a male child is unclean for seven days” (Leviticus 12:2). The birth of the flesh needs purification. The male child is the stronger sense.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Leviticus 12:2, applying the law about a woman who bears a male child to the soul's birth of a stronger spiritual sense.

title: Thirty-three days of purification
english: For thirty-three days she remains in the blood of her purification (Leviticus 12:4). This is a time of healing for the soul. She is not to hurry to holy things.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the purification period after childbirth from Leviticus 12, applying it to the soul's need for healing before approaching holy things.

title: Female birth doubles the purification days
english: If she gives birth to a female, the number is doubled. A weaker disposition demands longer care. Mercy adapts the times.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the purification periods after childbirth in Leviticus 12, applying them to the soul's healing.

title: The poor offering and Christ the lamb
english: A year-old lamb and a turtledove, or two turtledoves if the person is poor (Leviticus 12:6). Mary offered the gift of the poor (Luke 2:24). Christ is the lamb.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the offerings prescribed for a woman after childbirth, now turning to the poor's alternative and its fulfillment in Mary and Christ.

title: The priest discerns visible sin
english: A plague of leprosy in the skin is a fault in conduct that is open. The priest sees it and judges. Not every swelling is leprosy.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the law of leprosy in the skin to open faults in a person's way of life, which the priest must examine and judge.

title: Total confession makes clean
english: If leprosy covers the whole body and is white, the person is clean (Leviticus 13:13). Total confession makes a person white. The one who covers only part remains unclean.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical rule about leprosy to confession of sin: a leprosy that covers the whole body and turns white is clean, and so total confession makes a person clean.

title: Seven days of silence before judgment
english: The priest will shut him up for seven days. A testing of silence. Wait for the light of judgment.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the priest's seven-day quarantine of the unclean person as a figure of the soul's silent waiting before God's judgment.

title: The Leper's Exclusion
english: Torn clothes, bare head, outside the camp. Mourning of sin. Outside the peace of the church he who remains unclean.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical rule about the leper's torn clothes and uncovered head, applying it to the sinner who remains unclean and outside the peace of the church.

title: Leprosy in the garment as corruption in conduct or teaching
english: Leprosy in a garment is a fault in conduct or teaching. Burn what is incurable. The new garment of Christ.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical rules about leprosy in a garment, applying them to the moral and doctrinal life of the believer.

title: The priest declares clean when healing returns
english: The priest declares it clean when health returns. Christ absolves. Do not return to vomit (Proverbs 26:11; 2 Peter 2:22). Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is concluding his homily on the cleansing of leprosy, applying the priest's declaration of cleanness to Christ's absolution and warning against returning to sin.
